countries_thin_or_null: Nunavut — devolution agreement signed 2024 with transfer date April 2027; resource-revenue provisions exist but are not yet operational; no live edges beyond the agreement document itself

proposed_reports.title: Yukon Northern Affairs Program Devolution Transfer Agreement
proposed_reports.publisher: Government of Canada / Government of Yukon
proposed_reports.description: The 2001/2003 devolution agreement transferring administration and control of public lands, waters and non-renewable resources to the Yukon, including the resource-revenue sharing and TFF-offset provisions.

proposed_reports.title: Northwest Territories Lands and Resources Devolution Agreement
proposed_reports.publisher: Government of Canada / Government of the Northwest Territories / Aboriginal Parties
proposed_reports.description: The 2013/2014 devolution agreement transferring administration and control of public lands, waters and non-renewable resources to the NWT, defining Resource Revenues, Net Fiscal Benefit, and the offset against Territorial Formula Financing payments.

proposed_reports.title: Nunavut Lands and Resources Devolution Agreement
proposed_reports.publisher: Government of Canada / Government of Nunavut / Nunavut Tunngavik Incorporated
proposed_reports.description: The 2024 final devolution agreement transferring administration and control of public lands, freshwater and non-renewable resources to Nunavut, with a transfer date of 1 April 2027 and resource-revenue sharing provisions that interact with Territorial Formula Financing.

proposed_reports.title: Northwest Territories Intergovernmental Resource Revenue Sharing Agreement
proposed_reports.publisher: Government of the Northwest Territories / Aboriginal Parties
proposed_reports.description: Agreement under which the GNWT shares up to 25% of its Net Fiscal Benefit from resource revenues with participating Aboriginal governments, in addition to existing land-claim royalty shares.

dependencies.basis: Canada’s Territorial Formula Financing page and the Yukon devolution agreement itself state that natural-resource revenues are excluded from TFF eligible revenues and are instead governed by the separate devolution/resource-revenue-sharing arrangements.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Natural resource revenues are not part of territorial eligible revenues for the purposes of TFF calculations. The treatment of natural resource revenues is negotiated separately with each territory as part of overall negotiations on the devolution of the federal responsibility for the administration and control of onshore natural resources to the territorial governments. The Yukon and Northwest Territories Governments have completed devolution and resource revenue sharing agreements.

dependencies.basis: The NWT devolution agreement defines the Resource Revenues that are subject to offset against the Territorial Formula Financing Payment, and Canada’s TFF page confirms the exclusion of natural-resource revenues from the TFF calculation in favour of the devolution arrangements.
dependencies.evidence_quote: “Net Fiscal Benefit” means the amount of Resource Revenues that is not offset against the Territorial Formula Financing Payment pursuant to sections 10.2 and 10.3.

dependencies.basis: NWT budget and Public Accounts documents reference the devolution agreement’s resource-revenue sharing and the resulting reduction in the Territorial Formula Financing Grant.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Half of resource revenues are shared with the federal government by reducing the Territorial Formula Financing Grant payments from Canada to the Government of the Northwest Territories.

dependencies.basis: NWT fiscal documents record the net fiscal benefit transfer to Indigenous government signatories under the intergovernmental resource-revenue sharing arrangement.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Net Fiscal Benefit Transfer to Indigenous Government Signatories ... Contribution to NWT Heritage Fund

dependencies.basis: Canada’s TFF page notes that negotiations with Nunavut on the treatment of natural-resource revenues are ongoing; the 2024 Nunavut devolution agreement now supplies the framework that will govern those revenues once the April 2027 transfer occurs.
dependencies.evidence_quote: Negotiations with the Government of Nunavut are ongoing.

dependencies.evidence_quote: All figures are derived from Statistics Canada, Table 18-10-0004-01: Consumer Price Index, monthly, not seasonally adjusted. ... Data for the northern territorial capitals are compiled by the Nunavut Bureau of Statistics from the same Statistics Canada source.
